quandoUsar: Lists where pulling down is the expected gesture on mobile, such as an inbox, a feed, or notifications.
An area with its own scrolling inside a panel or an app frame (`height`), which refreshes the content without reloading the page.
Updates that sometimes start outside the gesture, from a button or a timer: `refreshing` shows the same refresh state.
quandoEvitar: It does not suit a whole page scrolling on the `body`: the gesture only exists inside its own container, which needs a height.
Use `infinite-masonry` when new content should arrive on scrolling to the end, not on pulling the top.
Use `message-scroller` for conversations, where new content arrives at the end of the list.

teclado.acao: The component's first focus stop is the `refreshLabel` button (default “Refresh”), which only appears with keyboard focus; the next `Tab` goes to the scroll area.
On the button, triggers the same `onRefresh` as the gesture; during the refresh it is `aria-disabled` and does not repeat.
With focus on the scroll area, scroll the content (native behavior).

acessibilidade: The scroll area is `role="region"`, focusable, with `aria-busy` during the refresh; replace the generic name from `label` (default “Content”) with the name of the list.
A `role="status"` region announces “Refreshing” and “Updated” (fixed in English in the code), and the visual indicator is `aria-hidden`.
movimento: The content follows the finger 1:1 at the start and with increasing resistance up to `maxPull`; the indicator appears, grows, the arrow flips and, past `threshold`, it stretches into a capsule in the accent color.
On release past the limit, the content holds at up to 56 px while the indicator spins; when the Promise finishes, a checkmark appears for 0.65 s and everything returns with a no-overshoot spring.
With “reduce motion”, the returns become jumps, the icons only fade, and the spin slows down (2.4 s per turn).
responsivo: It fills the parent's height by default; if the parent has no defined height, pass `height` so the area can scroll.
`overscroll-behavior` prevents the pull from passing to the page and triggering the browser's own reload on mobile.
desempenho: The pull animates a single motion value (transform), with no React re-render on every frame; touch uses a non-passive listener so it can block scrolling only during the gesture.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/pull-to-refresh/pull-to-refresh`. `onRefresh` should return a Promise: the indicator spins until it finishes; without a Promise, it spins for 0.6 s.
Give the component a height (`height` or a parent with a height) and put the list inside it: it is itself the scrolling area.
On desktop, dragging with the mouse is not obvious; also keep a visible button that calls the same function and show the state with `refreshing`.
